extracted.intended_audience: Firefox users and people interested in Pocket's recommended reading in the Firefox new tab
extracted.subtask_description: Explains how Pocket curates and surfaces recommended articles in Firefox's new tab, including what kinds of stories are chosen, how curation works, privacy expectations, and how users can save articles for later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story quality: unexpected perspectives, intriguing profiles, absorbing deep-dives
rubrics_metrics.description: Pocket helps you discover and save stories you actually want to read—unexpected perspectives, intriguing profiles, and absorbing deep-dives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pocket focuses on surfacing the 'best of the web' rather than every published piece; emphasis is on compelling, in-depth, or surprising content that is 'worth reading'. This is the editorial ideal used to select stories shown in the new tab.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curation sources and signals: user recommendations plus editorial selection
rubrics_metrics.description: We have 30+ million global users helping guide the curation process by pointing to high-quality stories published on sites all across the internet. Our editors then sift through the most-recommended and most-read stories and handpick the best to share with you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is driven first by community signals (most-recommended, most-read) aggregated from Pocket's large user base, and then by human editors who handpick from that pool. Both popularity metrics and editorial judgment determine what appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation frequency and variety: daily refreshed selection
rubrics_metrics.description: We rotate through a selection of new articles every day, so it’s like a little surprise each time you open a new tab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content is refreshed daily to provide variety and new discoveries rather than showing the same items repeatedly; this is a product-level commitment to freshness and serendipity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy standard: browsing data remains local to Firefox
rubrics_metrics.description: Rest assured, your browsing data never leaves your personal copy of Firefox—neither Mozilla nor Pocket ever receives a copy of your browser history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pocket emphasizes that recommendation and curation occur without sending users' browser history to Mozilla/Pocket. The post points readers to Pocket’s FAQ for more privacy and curation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saveability and account requirement: can save recommendations to your Pocket list
rubrics_metrics.description: See that little Pocket icon into your Firefox toolbar? Activate your Firefox account, and you can click that icon—or the three-dots menu on any story in your new tab—and save a story to come back to later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To use the save-for-later feature, users must activate their Firefox account. Saved stories are collected in a tidy list for later reading, supporting time-flexible consumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeless discoverability: promoting stories regardless of original publication date
rubrics_metrics.description: Pocket provides a place where such stories can continue to thrive no matter when they were first published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Curation is not limited to newly published pieces; editors and recommendation signals surface high-quality content even if it was published earlier, prioritizing value over recency alone.
